content_units: Best Laptop Picks for a CS Student

All four meet your   16 GB RAM minimum   and stay within the   $1,200 cap  . Based on your priorities—  battery life first, then light weight, then staying on budget  —the strongest overall pick is the   MacBook Air M2  , with the   Acer Swift 14   as the best Windows-balanced alternative.
Ranked Laptop Comparison
Rank   Laptop   Price   Weight   Claimed Battery   Storage   Best For   Main Tradeoff
1   MacBook Air M2   USD 1,199   1.24 kg   15 hours   256 GB SSD   Best battery + portability + long-term value   Very limited storage; macOS may not fit every CS workflow
2   Acer Swift 14   USD 999   1.3 kg   14 hours   512 GB SSD   Best Windows all-rounder for student use   CPU is less performance-oriented than the Ryzen 7 option
3   Lenovo IdeaPad Pro 5   USD 1,099   1.46 kg   10 hours   1 TB SSD   Best coding performance/storage balance   Heavier and weaker battery than top two
4   ASUS Vivobook 15   USD 849   1.7 kg   8 hours   512 GB SSD   Lowest-cost option   Heaviest and shortest battery life
Top Picks and Tradeoffs
Option 1:   MacBook Air M2     Best overall if battery life and portability matter most     1.24 kg / 15 hr / $1,199
-   Coding:   Excellent for programming, web dev, Python, Java, Unix-based tooling, and general CS coursework. Strong keyboard, silent design, and great standby behavior.
-   Portability:   Best in this list. It is the   lightest   and has the   best claimed battery life  .
-   Long-term value:   Strong resale value, premium build, and typically ages well.
-   Tradeoff:     256 GB SSD   is tight for local VMs, Docker images, datasets, Android Studio projects, or dual-toolchain setups. Also, some Windows-specific coursework may require workarounds.
Compare specs
Option 2:   Acer Swift 14     Best Windows choice for balanced student use     1.3 kg / 14 hr / $999
-   Coding:   Very solid for general CS work, IDEs, browser-heavy workflows, Python, Java, and light local development.
-   Portability:   Nearly as light as the MacBook and close on battery claims, making it highly practical for campus use.
-   Long-term value:   Good value at   $999  , leaving budget room for a monitor, external SSD, or warranty.
-   Tradeoff:   Not as much raw multi-core headroom or storage as the Lenovo, so it is less ideal if you expect heavier compile workloads or large project files.
View Acer line
Option 3:   Lenovo IdeaPad Pro 5     Best if coding performance and storage matter more than battery     1.46 kg / 10 hr / $1,099
-   Coding:   Probably the strongest choice here for heavier dev workloads thanks to   Ryzen 7   plus   1 TB SSD  .
-   Portability:   Still portable, but clearly less travel-friendly than the top two.
-   Long-term value:   The extra storage is a real advantage for CS students who keep local repos, containers, datasets, and dev tools.
-   Tradeoff:   Battery life is notably weaker than the MacBook Air and Acer Swift, which matters if you spend long days away from outlets.
View IdeaPad line
Option 4:   ASUS Vivobook 15     Best budget saver, but weakest fit for your priorities     1.7 kg / 8 hr / $849
-   Coding:   16 GB RAM and Core i7 are enough for everyday student coding.
-   Portability:   This is the least portable option because it is the   heaviest   and has the shortest claimed battery.
-   Long-term value:   Good upfront value, but less aligned with your battery/weight priorities, so the lower price may not feel worth it over time.
-   Tradeoff:   More of a budget productivity laptop than an ideal carry-all-day CS machine.
View Vivobook line
Final Recommendation for Your Priorities
1.   MacBook Air M2   — best match if you want the most portable laptop with the strongest battery life and best long-term ownership value.
2.   Acer Swift 14   — best pick if you want a safer   Windows   choice without giving up much portability or battery.
3.   Lenovo IdeaPad Pro 5   — best trade-off if you value   storage and stronger coding performance   more than all-day unplugged use.
4.   ASUS Vivobook 15   — only worth choosing if   saving money   matters more than weight and battery.
